subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw enforce a default Docker sandbox `pidsLimit` of 1024 for existing unset configs, and what validated opt-out value should ship with it?
rationale: This is a security hardening change, but it also changes existing upgrade behavior and the current schema/type/docs disagree on Docker-default or unlimited opt-out semantics.

options.title: Approve default cap with explicit opt-out
options.body: Use 1024 or another approved cap by default, update schema/type docs and public docs to document the opt-out, and require focused tests plus real Docker proof before merge.

options.title: Choose a different default or staged rollout
options.body: Pick a different cap or a warning/doctor-first migration path if maintainers think 1024 is too likely to break existing workloads.

options.title: Defer the runtime default
options.body: Keep current runtime behavior and resolve the security concern through docs/doctor guidance until a broader resource-limit policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve default cap with explicit opt-out
recommendation.body: Use 1024 or another approved cap by default, update schema/type docs and public docs to document the opt-out, and require focused tests plus real Docker proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox security hardening history makes Peter Steinberger the strongest individual routing candidate for the default and opt-out decision.
